source_title: Finnish police launch criminal investigation into Google’s planned $15 billion data centre site - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Finnish law enforcement authorities announced on Thursday (October 29) that they have opened a criminal investigation into suspected environmental law violations at the construction site of a planned Google data center in northern Finland. According to news agency Reuters, the site is a key component of Alphabet-owned Google’s massive $15 billion artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure plan unveiled last month – an initiative the US tech giant characterised as its single largest investment in Europe.According to authorities, Google subsidiary Tuike Finland initiated forest clearing and land drainage operations near the town of Muhos before completing the mandatory environmental impact assessments required under Finnish law. A Google spokesperson stated that the firm will cooperate fully with law enforcement and will remain focused on upholding compliance across all of its properties.Police investigate drainage and water managementThe investigation centers on whether earthworks and water control methods at the development breached national water regulations.“We are investigating whether the company's operations have breached the water act and resulted in environmental damage,” Detective Superintendent Kari Pakanen was quoted as saying. Pakanen noted that if the company is found guilty, the case could result in a corporate fine, though he declined to say whether individual employees or executives could become targets of the inquiry.In an official statement, police reported that preliminary findings revealed ambiguities and shortcomings regarding water management and drainage on the Tuike property. Authorities plan to release an update in December, but indicated the full investigation will extend into 2027.The police probe follows regulatory intervention earlier in the month. On October 6, Finland's Supervisory Agency (LVV), which is the administrative body responsible for overseeing environmental permits and assessments, ordered Google to immediately suspend all preparatory work that alters the natural environment at the Muhos plot and an additional separate location.Pakanen noted that determining whether permits will be granted to restart work remains strictly the jurisdiction of the LVV. An LVV spokesperson stated it is currently unclear how long it will take to determine whether those permits will be issued.“We've partnered closely with the government and communities in Finland on infrastructure for over a decade, and are actively responding to enquiries from LVV and other authorities,” Google's spokesperson said.Meanwhile, Finland has established itself as one of Europe’s leading hubs for tech infrastructure, thanks to its cold northern climate, low-carbon power grid, and active government backing for AI initiatives. Despite covering an area comparable to Germany, Finland is home to fewer than 6 million people and has historically encountered less local pushback against large-scale computing facilities than regions like the United States.Google’s broader infrastructure program in the country is planned to encompass data centers, power grid upgrades, and clean energy and battery storage systems designed to handle computing loads for core products, including Gemini, Search, Google Maps and YouTube.However, the rapid expansion is placing new demands on national infrastructure. State grid operator Fingrid has projected that domestic electricity consumption could jump by up to 40% in the coming years if all contracted data center grid connections move forward.
